name: 2024 US East & Gulf Coast ILA Dockworkers Port Strike
severity_rationale: 45,000 dockworkers represented by the International Longshoremen's Association (ILA) struck across 36 container ports along the US Atlantic and Gulf Coasts, halting approximately 50% of total US maritime ocean import/export trade. Shippers faced immediate component delays and ocean carriers implemented emergency congestion surcharges of $1,000 to $3,000 per container.
source_org: United States Maritime Alliance (USMX) / ILA / CNBC Supply Chain
notes_on_facts: First coastwide ILA strike since 1977 commenced Oct 1, 2024. A tentative wage agreement suspended the strike late Oct 3, but anchor queues of dozens of container vessels required 2 to 3 weeks to clear backlogged import cargo.

events.headline: Dockworkers strike shuts 36 ports along US East and Gulf Coasts from Maine to Texas
events.summary: Master contract expiration triggers full labor walkout across 14 major port authorities, halting container gantry cranes and roll-on/roll-off automotive terminals.

events.headline: Vessel anchor queues expand off Savannah and New York, threatening manufacturing component shortages
events.summary: Marine terminals report growing queues of container vessels at anchor outside East Coast ports, with logistics operators warning of inventory dwell and electronic component delivery delays.
